title: A buffer drawn at one texel per pixel is one level off in some columns
body:
decade's compositor draws a client's buffer that is shown at exactly one texel per pixel with a small blend in some columns. una's `examples/canvas.rs` draws a checkerboard of single black and white pixels inside a magenta frame. Its `--verify` flag checks a capture pixel by pixel. Run inside a decade pane on 2026-11-26 and captured from the host output, it gave:

| | result |
|---|---|
| frame | whole on all four sides, 795 by 1155 pixels |
| squares | every one at the right place, with no column doubled or missing |
| wrong pixels | 19,055, all 254 where 255 belongs or 1 where 0 belongs |
| where | 20 whole columns, about 40 pixels apart (one gap of 29) |

A buffer drawn at a size other than its own would show grey columns under a linear filter, or a doubled column under nearest-neighbour sampling. Neither happened, so the size is right. The pattern fits a linear filter at one texel per pixel, where the texture coordinates drift by a few thousandths of a texel across the surface. Most columns land on texel centres and some do not. Hyprland 0.56.2 samples nearest-neighbour when it draws a surface at its buffer's size, and the same pane was exact there. Nobody has yet read decade's renderer to see where it sets the filter.

## Proposal

When decade draws a client surface at one texel per pixel, sample with nearest-neighbour. Keep linear filtering for surfaces it scales.
